articles.title: Impact of anatomical changes on simulated proton arc therapy and intensity-modulated proton therapy for lung cancer
articles.summary: This study demonstrates that simulated proton arc therapy (sPAT) provides superior robustness compared to intensity-modulated proton therapy (IMPT) when addressing inter-fractional anatomical changes in lung cancer patients. The findings highlight potential advantages for treatment planning in lung tumor sites prone to motion.

articles.title: Assessment of Radiation Dose and Volume Changes in the Masticatory Apparatus and their Clinical Correlation with Trismus in Oral Cavity Cancer Patients
articles.summary: Researchers analyzed the correlation between radiation dose, muscle atrophy, and trismus in oral cavity cancer patients. The study suggests that incorporating masticatory muscle sparing into radiation treatment planning is crucial to reducing long-term functional morbidity.

articles.title: Photon Versus Proton Whole-Body Irradiation Combined with Olaparib in C57BL/6 Mice
articles.summary: This study examines the multi-organ oxidative toxicity in mice following whole-body irradiation with either photons or protons, combined with the PARP inhibitor olaparib. The findings provide insights into potential differences in radiosensitizing effects and systemic toxicity between these two radiation modalities.

articles.title: Model-Based Normal Tissue Complication Probability Comparison Between Proton and Photon Therapies for Brain Tumors
articles.summary: This planning comparison study indicates that proton beam therapy may reduce the risk of secondary cancers in patients with brain tumors compared to IMRT, while photon therapy shows advantages regarding specific toxicities like blindness and brain necrosis. The study emphasizes the value of using radiotherapy treatment planning guidelines for objective clinical comparison.

articles.title: Clinical Outcomes and Safety of Spatially Fractionated Radiotherapy for Malignant Tumors
articles.summary: A systematic review evaluating the clinical outcomes and safety profiles of spatially fractionated radiotherapy (SFRT) across various malignant tumors. The report highlights the current evidence base and identifies key considerations for the use of this technique in clinical practice.

articles.title: Six-year data from three magnetic resonance-guided radiotherapy systems demonstrate long-term stability of linear accelerator quality assurance
articles.summary: This study analyzed six years of data from three MR-guided radiotherapy systems to assess the long-term stability of quality assurance programs. The results support a potential reconsideration of traditional QA schedules based on the demonstrated performance consistency.

articles.title: Preliminary evaluation of ProSpare for rectal protection in prostate bed radiotherapy
articles.summary: Results from the multicenter POPS trial indicate that the use of a rectal obturator, ProSpare, during prostate bed radiotherapy leads to a measurable reduction in acute bowel toxicity. Patient-reported outcomes and dosimetric improvements support its potential utility in clinical settings.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence, Multi-Omics, and Multimodal Integration in Precision Radiotherapy for Head and Neck Cancer
articles.summary: This review explores how integrating AI, multi-omics, and multimodal clinical data can enhance precision in radiotherapy for head and neck cancers. It discusses the current state of research and the challenges of linking these technologies to clinical decision-making.

articles.title: DoseRAD2026: A benchmark dataset for AI-accelerated photon and proton dose calculation in radiotherapy
articles.summary: This article introduces the DoseRAD2026 benchmark dataset designed to support research in fast and accurate dose calculation for both CT and MRI-guided radiotherapy. The dataset aims to facilitate the development of AI-driven solutions for real-time adaptive treatment planning.

articles.title: Dose-Informed Surgical Margin in Mandibular Osteoradionecrosis Surgery: Integrating Radiation Biology into Osteotomy Planning
articles.summary: This study explores moving beyond anatomical landmarks by integrating radiation biology into surgical planning for mandibular osteoradionecrosis. The researchers aim to improve outcomes for head and neck radiotherapy patients through more biologically informed surgical margins.

articles.title: Diagnostic CT-Based Palliative Radiotherapy Using kV Image Verification: A Prospective Feasibility Study
articles.summary: This feasibility study investigates the use of existing diagnostic CT scans for palliative radiotherapy planning instead of dedicated simulation CTs. The workflow, utilizing kV image verification, aims to increase access and efficiency for patients with bone metastases.

articles.title: A novel automatic real-time motion tracking method in MRI-guided radiotherapy
articles.summary: Researchers have developed an automatic real-time markerless motion tracking method for MRI-guided radiotherapy (MRIgRT). The study demonstrates high precision in tracking and segmentation, suggesting significant potential for improving radiotherapy efficacy.

articles.title: Curative-intent management of de novo metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma: an evidence-based consensus guideline from the International Collaborating Oncology Organisations
articles.summary: An international panel of 54 experts developed consensus guidelines for managing de novo metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma, highlighting the shift toward curative-intent protocols. The recommendations integrate modern systemic therapy with targeted local radiation strategies to improve long-term survival outcomes.

articles.title: Preclinical highlights from the 64th Annual Meeting of the Particle Therapy Co-Operative Group (PTCOG 64)
articles.summary: This summary of PTCOG 64 highlights a shift in particle therapy toward integrating advanced imaging, biological modeling, and patient-specific decision support. Experts identified digital twins and biologically optimized multi-ion therapy as key innovations for the next generation of precision treatment.

articles.title: Charge collection efficiency in air-vented plane-parallel ionisation chambers at ultra-high dose rates
articles.summary: This study develops a Monte Carlo framework to investigate ion recombination and space-charge effects in ionization chambers during FLASH radiotherapy. The work provides essential modeling data for ensuring accurate dosimetry in ultra-high dose rate environments.

articles.title: Clinical and Geometric Evaluation of Artificial Intelligence-based Organ at Risk Auto-contouring for Post-operative Oral Tongue Cancer Radiotherapy
articles.summary: Research into AI-based organ-at-risk segmentation for oral tongue cancer shows high geometric accuracy and significant workflow efficiency improvements. While auto-contouring maintains dosimetric integrity for most organs, the study emphasizes the necessity of manual verification for serial structures like the spinal cord.

articles.title: Feasibility of Urethra-Sparing Ultra-Hypofractionated Three-Dose-Level Radiotherapy for Prostate Cancer
articles.summary: This planning study evaluates a three-dose-level ultra-hypofractionated approach for prostate cancer patients where a lesion is close to the urethra. Results indicate that target coverage can be maintained while adhering to strict organ-at-risk constraints.

articles.title: ESTRO-EPTN guidelines for independent dose calculation and log file-based patient-specific quality assurance in scanned particle therapy
articles.summary: The European Society for Radiotherapy and Oncology (ESTRO) and the European Particle Therapy Network (EPTN) have released new guidelines for independent dose calculation and log file-based quality assurance in particle therapy. These recommendations are intended to standardize safety protocols across centers while maintaining rigorous machine QA standards.
